entries.name: traceBackward, after a cited spec is renamed.recognises a backticked name by a spec name's shape: an M-name is one, a camel-cased name is not
traceBackward, after a cited spec is renamed.still lists a criterion citation of the spec, and says it is missing, rather than dropping it
traceBackward, where a line names an artifact in code rather than a comment.makes no link from a string, and still links a comment, trailing or above
traceBackward, where a link was made before its artifact existed.shows the link as suspect, with no version linked, and says why
traceBackward, where git cannot read part of the repository.names a file git cannot read, in git's words, and still answers from the rest
traceBackward, where git cannot read part of the repository.refuses a submodule in words, since it is no file
traceBackward.gives a criterion's own version, not its spec's: the last commit that changed its text
traceBackward.links a test file to the criteria a spec's Tests table names it for, a bare name included, and the nested node to it
traceBackward.lists the links in order of trust: source path, Tests table, the code, the commit's message, its trailers
traceBackward.marks a link suspect once the artifact's own text changed after the link was made, and only that one
traceBackward.names a source it cannot read, and why, and still answers from the rest; HEAD by default
traceBackward.names the commit it read and the line, with the commit that last changed the line
traceBackward.never guesses which of several files a bare test name means, and says so
traceBackward.reads every source, and says of each link how it is known: only an architecture source path is recorded
traceBackward.refers to each artifact by its path and the commit of the version linked, with that commit's date and time
traceBackward.refuses, in words, a file absent at the commit, a line out of range, an unknown commit, and a directory that is no repository
traceBackward.says a cited artifact that does not exist is missing, rather than dropping it
traceBackward.says a line that traces to nothing is untraced, and guesses nothing
traceBackward.takes code citations only from the lines in scope: the line's own block, its enclosing lines' blocks, and the file's opening block
